briefing.opening: Good morning/afternoon. Welcome to the 2026-08-10 Climate Briefing.

sections.title: 🔴 Unprecedented Climate Crisis, An Era of Compound Disasters
sections.content: Last month, global ocean temperatures reached an all-time high, signaling an acceleration of global warming [2, 8, 20, 29, 35, 38, 46, 49, 161]. Domestically, 'compound disasters,' where extreme heatwaves follow severe torrential rains, have increased more than threefold compared to the past 30 years, threatening the lives of citizens [3, 15, 26, 28, 34, 45]. In Europe, economic damages from record-breaking heatwaves are snowballing, causing severe impacts such as nuclear power plant shutdowns and transportation disruptions [5, 6, 29, 53, 163, 168, 171, 172, 177, 181]. Heatwaves accelerate biological aging [16, 40], and thousands have been evacuated due to uncontrollable wildfires in Canada, illustrating the harsh reality of climate change unfolding before our eyes worldwide [183]. Concerns are also being raised that food and energy crises could deepen, with domestic crops like 'Ilcheongung' suffering damage due to climate change [4, 22].

sections.title: 🌱 Domestic and International Efforts and Progress in Responding to Climate Change
sections.content: To raise awareness about the severity of climate change, the 'Climate Change Science Quiz Competition' hosted by the Korea Meteorological Administration successfully concluded [1, 9, 12, 30], and educational and cultural activities are vibrant, such as the opening of the 'Scenes of Climate' exhibition at the National Assembly Busan Library [7]. In preparation for heatwaves and torrential rains, practical adaptation efforts are ongoing, including river maintenance in Incheon City, the emergence of high-performance windows, and the passage of the 'Climate Insurance Introduction Act' and 'Climate Crisis Adaptation Act' by the National Assembly's Special Committee on Climate [13, 14, 23, 24, 25, 31, 37, 39, 44, 48]. Innovative attempts to respond to climate change are also being made in the agricultural sector, such as the creation of smart orchards in Seosan City, education on region-specific onion cultivation techniques in Anseong City, and verification of the possibility of open-field cultivation of Jeju citrus fruits [11, 18, 19]. Movements encouraging carbon neutrality in daily life are also spreading, such as the Korea Climate Change Research Institute's 'Computer and Lights OFF' challenge [10, 76] and Kiwoom Securities' 'Step Donation' campaign [56, 75, 97].

sections.title: ⚠️ Accelerating Renewable Energy Transition and Current Challenges
sections.content: Domestic company E-REM is expanding its renewable energy generation and ESS (Energy Storage System) businesses by acquiring Wonpick E&C [98, 99, 100, 105, 109, 113, 117, 147, 153], and Gyeonggi Province is publicly soliciting 21.9 billion won for renewable energy projects in the upstream Paldang region, demonstrating ongoing efforts to expand renewable energy [101, 112, 119, 120, 125, 126, 129, 133, 137, 141, 145, 149]. However, in Southeast Asia, half of renewable energy projects are being stranded due to grid bottlenecks [121], and domestically, concerns about indiscriminate development are growing, with a bill proposed to regulate setback distances to prevent the proliferation of renewable energy facilities around Garorim Bay Marine Ecological Park [108, 110, 115, 116, 118, 124, 131, 135, 136, 143, 146, 150, 154]. The village of Moerdijk near the Port of Rotterdam in the Netherlands is facing an existential crisis due to wind power expansion [162], suggesting the importance of seeking coexistence strategies with local communities when introducing eco-friendly energy facilities. Furthermore, the controversy that Amazon's AI data centers emit 33 million tons of carbon annually [78] demonstrates that energy efficiency and carbon emission management are essential in the era of digital transformation.

sections.title: 🇰🇷 Transition to a Carbon-Neutral Society: Policy and Citizen Participation
sections.content: Domestically and internationally, various policy efforts are underway to achieve carbon neutrality, and the Carbon Neutrality Framework Act Review Subcommittee of the National Assembly's Special Committee on Climate is holding discussions to deliberate on related bills in depth [84, 85, 94]. Local community participation is active, with Gwangmyeong City and small business owners expanding 'Climate Volunteer Affiliates' and practicing carbon neutrality in daily life through electronic receipt issuance [59, 60, 61, 65, 68, 71, 79, 80, 87], and Jincheon County emerging as a hub for carbon-neutral green growth [58, 72, 73, 82, 86, 91]. Youth are evaluating the current Carbon Neutrality Act as 'a 60-point act' and urging the National Assembly to revise it [55, 64], emphasizing the need for future generations' voices to be significantly reflected in policy decisions. Meanwhile, the first report card on basic local governments' carbon neutrality plans points out a lack of scientific basis [66], highlighting the importance of establishing more concrete and effective plans to achieve carbon neutrality goals.

briefing.closing: Today's briefing once again reminds us of the diverse domestic and international efforts continuing amidst an unprecedented climate crisis, the challenges of renewable energy transition, and the importance of policy and civic participation for transitioning to a carbon-neutral society. This concludes the 2026-08-10 Climate Briefing.
